title: Longest Run of Ones With k Flips
statement:
The array bits holds only 0s and 1s. You may turn at most k of the zeros into ones.

Return the length of the longest contiguous run of ones you can end up with.

examples.why: Flip the zeros at indexes 4 and 5: indexes 2 to 8 become seven ones in a row.
Flipping the first zero gives only 3. Flipping the zero at index 7 joins 1, 1, 1 with the last 1 for 5.
No flips allowed and no ones at all, so the longest run is empty.

hints: Turn the question around: what is the longest stretch that contains at most k zeros?
Grow a window to the right one element at a time and count the zeros inside. When does the window become invalid, and what is the cheapest fix?
When the zero count exceeds k, move the left edge right until one zero has left. Record the window length after every step.

explain.intuition:
Flipping zeros inside a stretch makes it all ones, so the real question is: what is the longest contiguous stretch that contains at most k zeros? Which zeros to flip then follows from the stretch.

That is a classic sliding window. Extend the right edge one element at a time and count zeros. If the count goes above k, the window is too greedy, so move the left edge right until a zero drops out. Both edges only move forward, so each element enters and leaves the window once. It is like a debounce window that slides over a stream of events instead of restarting.
steps: For each right: if bits[right] is 0, add one to zeros.
While zeros > k: if bits[left] is 0, subtract one from zeros; move left right.
pitfalls: Greedily flipping the first k zeros you meet. The second example shows the best zeros to flip can be further on.
Resetting the window to start at right when it breaks. That throws away ones that could still be part of the next run.
Forgetting the case k = 0, where the answer is just the longest run of ones, possibly 0.

solutions.title: Check every start
solutions.idea: From each start, extend right while at most k zeros have been seen.

solutions.title: Sliding window with a zero count
solutions.idea: Grow the window on the right; when it holds more than k zeros, shrink it from the left until it is valid again.

followups: The window never needs to shrink, only slide: move left by one at most per step. Why is the final window size still the answer?
The bits arrive as an endless stream and k is small. How would you report the best run so far using O(k) memory?
